</span></span>
</span></td></tr>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.SSSx1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSSx1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">I call this prompt type “prefilled”, because the behavior matching or non-matching token is already prefilled after the prompt. This prompt type is the same as used in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">Panickssery et al. (2024)</a></cite> and <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tan et al. (2024)</a></cite>. For training steering vectors, I use 250 samples per vector, based on my convergence experiments shown in Section <a href="#S5.SS1" title="5.1 Convergence analysis of steering vectors ‣ 5 Results" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.1</span></a>. In Section <a href="#S4.SS11" title="4.11 Prompt types ‣ 4 Methods and Experimental Setup" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.11</span></a>, I introduce steering-vector training-data variations that leverage in-context learning <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Brown et al., 2020b</a>)</cite> to elicit behavior representations.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3.SSSx2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection">Recording model activations</h4>

<div id="S4.SS3.SSSx2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSSx2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The language model processes the positive and negative training samples in two separate forward passes. I record the internal model activations that generate the next token after the prefilled answer token “A” or “B”, which is likely to be “)”. Specifically, I store the output of the <math id="S4.SS3.SSSx2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>l</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l</annotation></semantics></math>-th transformer decoder block, which is the vector produced after that block’s self-attention and feed-forward sub-layers are applied. This output, often referred to as the residual stream at layer <math id="S4.SS3.SSSx2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>l</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l</annotation></semantics></math>, is the activation that is passed to the next block <math id="S4.SS3.SSSx2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l+1</annotation></semantics></math>. I denote the activation recorded at this specific point for the positive sample as <math id="S4.SS3.SSSx2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{a}^{l}(x,y^{+})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐚</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{a}^{l}(x,y^{+})</annotation></semantics></math> and for the negative sample as <math id="S4.SS3.SSSx2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{a}^{l}(x,y^{-})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐚</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{a}^{l}(x,y^{-})</annotation></semantics></math>. I call these activations the positive activation and the negative activation, respectively, and say that I record the activation at token position of these differing answer tokens <span id="S4.SS3.SSSx2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#228B22;">B</span> and <span id="S4.SS3.SSSx2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#FF0000;">A</span>. The core idea of steering vectors is that the vector difference between two answer representations—in the myopia example, choosing the myopic answer versus the non-myopic answer—captures how the model represents myopic behavior internally at layer <math id="S4.SS3.SSSx2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>l</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l</annotation></semantics></math>. Following <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tan et al. (2024)</a></cite>, I record residual stream activations for Llama 2-7B-Chat at layer <math id="S4.SS3.SSSx2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l=13" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>13</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l=13</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3.SSSx3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection">Steering vector computation</h4>

<div id="S4.SS3.SSSx3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSSx3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The CAA steering vector <math id="S4.SS3.SSSx3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{s}^{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝐬</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{s}^{l}</annotation></semantics></math> is computed as the mean difference between these recorded activations from the positive (behavior-matching) and negative (behavior-non-matching) samples over the training dataset <math id="S4.SS3.SSSx3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}_{\text{train}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mtext>train</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}_{\text{train}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Specifically, using the <em id="S4.SS3.SSSx3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">prefilled</em> prompt type as in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">Panickssery et al. (2024)</a></cite> and <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tan et al. (2024)</a></cite>, the steering vector is:</p>
<table id="S4.Ex2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{s}^{l}=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{D}_{\text{train}}|}\sum_{(x_{i},y^{+}_{i},y^{-}_{i})\in\mathcal{D}_{\text{train}}}\bigl[\mathbf{a}^{l}(x_{i},y^{+}_{i})-\mathbf{a}^{l}(x_{i},y^{-}_{i})\bigr]\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{e}}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐬</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mtext>train</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mtext>train</mtext></msub></mrow></munder><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">[</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>𝐚</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msup><mi>𝐚</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi></msub></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{s}^{l}=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{D}_{\text{train}}|}\sum_{(x_{i},y^{+}_{i},y^{-}_{i})\in\mathcal{D}_{\text{train}}}\bigl[\mathbf{a}^{l}(x_{i},y^{+}_{i})-\mathbf{a}^{l}(x_{i},y^{-}_{i})\bigr]\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{e}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F4.fig1" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_minipage ltx_align_center ltx_align_middle" style="width:165.6pt;">
<div id="S4.F4.fig1.3" class="ltx_block ltx_figure_panel ltx_minipage ltx_align_center ltx_align_middle" style="width:172.5pt;"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.17881v1/caa_steering_vector_computation_conceptual.svg" id="S4.F4.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:238/178;" width="238" height="178"></object>
</div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F4.fig1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 4</span>: </span><span id="S4.F4.fig1.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Illustrating CAA steering vector computation in a favorable scenario: A 2D projection at layer <math id="S4.F4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>l</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l</annotation></semantics></math> shows distinct positive and negative activation clusters. This allows the steering vector <math id="S4.F4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{s}^{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝐬</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{s}^{l}</annotation></semantics></math> to accurately approximate individual activation differences. The means of positive and negative activations are <math id="S4.F4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,+}=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{D}_{\text{train}}|}\sum\mathbf{a}^{l}(x_{i},y^{+}_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝝁</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">+</mo></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mtext>train</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>∑</mo><mrow><msup><mi>𝐚</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,+}=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{D}_{\text{train}}|}\sum\mathbf{a}^{l}(x_{i},y^{+}_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.F4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,-}=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{D}_{\text{train}}|}\sum\mathbf{a}^{l}(x_{i},y^{-}_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝝁</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mtext>train</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>∑</mo><mrow><msup><mi>𝐚</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,-}=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{D}_{\text{train}}|}\sum\mathbf{a}^{l}(x_{i},y^{-}_{i})</annotation></semantics></math>, respectively. The steering vector can be computed as the difference between these means <math id="S4.F4.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{s}^{l}=\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,+}-\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,-}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐬</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>𝝁</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">+</mo></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>𝝁</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{s}^{l}=\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,+}-\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,-}</annotation></semantics></math>, which is equivalent to the previous definition as the mean of paired activation differences.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3.SSSx4" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection">Applying steering vectors</h4>

<div id="S4.SS3.SSSx4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSSx4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To steer the model’s behavior during inference, this computed steering vector <math id="S4.SS3.SSSx4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{s}^{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝐬</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{s}^{l}</annotation></semantics></math>, scaled by a multiplier <math id="S4.SS3.SSSx4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>λ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda</annotation></semantics></math>, is added to the output of the <math id="S4.SS3.SSSx4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>l</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l</annotation></semantics></math>-th transformer decoder block. The intervention is applied at every inference-step for autoregressive text generation. This transformation can be represented as a function <math id="S4.SS3.SSSx4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f^{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>f</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{l}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S4.Ex3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f^{l}:\mathbb{R}^{d_{e}}\to\mathbb{R}^{d_{e}},\quad\mathbf{a}\mapsto\mathbf{a}+\lambda\cdot\mathbf{s}^{l}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi></msub></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi></msub></msup></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>𝐚</mi><mo stretchy="false">↦</mo><mrow><mi>𝐚</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msup><mi>𝐬</mi><mi>l</mi></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{l}:\mathbb{R}^{d_{e}}\to\mathbb{R}^{d_{e}},\quad\mathbf{a}\mapsto\mathbf{a}+\lambda\cdot\mathbf{s}^{l}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.SSSx4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSSx4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">I call the steering multiplier <math id="S4.SS3.SSSx4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>λ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda</annotation></semantics></math> the steering strength, and applying steering vectors as steering the model. Unless otherwise specified, I use a steering multiplier <math id="S4.SS3.SSSx4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda=1</annotation></semantics></math> and intervene at layer <math id="S4.SS3.SSSx4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l=13" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>13</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l=13</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.4 </span>Evaluation of steering success</h3>

<div id="S4.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To ensure rigorous and unbiased evaluation of the CAA steering vector’s performance, I evaluate steering on held-out test sets <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}_{\text{test}}=\{x_{i}\}^{\mathbb{N}_{\text{test}}}_{i=1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mtext>test</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><msub><mi>ℕ</mi><mtext>test</mtext></msub></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}_{\text{test}}=\{x_{i}\}^{\mathbb{N}_{\text{test}}}_{i=1}</annotation></semantics></math> of plain prompts.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<div id="S4.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:345.0pt;">
<p id="S4.SS4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left"><span id="S4.SS4.p2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Test sample</span></p>
<p id="S4.SS4.p2.1.2" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left"><span id="S4.SS4.p2.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">We can give you 10 dollars now or 100 dollars after one week of waiting. What would you prefer?
</span></p>
<p id="S4.SS4.p2.1.3" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left"><span id="S4.SS4.p2.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Choices: 
<br class="ltx_break">(A) 100 dollars after a week 
<br class="ltx_break">(B) 10 dollars right now
</span></p>
<p id="S4.SS4.p2.1.4" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left"><span id="S4.SS4.p2.1.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Answer: (
</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS4.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The dataset samples used for training <math id="S4.SS4.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}_{\text{train}}=\{(\mathbf{x}_{i},y^{+}_{i},y^{-}_{i})\mid i\in[\mathbb{N}_{\text{train}}]\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mtext>train</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>ℕ</mi><mtext>train</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}_{\text{train}}=\{(\mathbf{x}_{i},y^{+}_{i},y^{-}_{i})\mid i\in[\mathbb{N}_{\text{train}}]\}</annotation></semantics></math> and testing <math id="S4.SS4.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}_{\text{test}}=\{\mathbf{x}_{i}\mid i\in[\mathbb{N}_{\text{test}}]\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mtext>test</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>ℕ</mi><mtext>test</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}_{\text{test}}=\{\mathbf{x}_{i}\mid i\in[\mathbb{N}_{\text{test}}]\}</annotation></semantics></math> are kept strictly separate. This means that the set of all input prompts from the steering vector training data <math id="S4.SS4.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\mathbf{x}_{i}\mid(\mathbf{x}_{i},y^{+}_{i},y^{-}_{i})\in\mathcal{D}_{\text{train}}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mtext>train</mtext></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\mathbf{x}_{i}\mid(\mathbf{x}_{i},y^{+}_{i},y^{-}_{i})\in\mathcal{D}_{\text{train}}\}</annotation></semantics></math> and the set of input samples from the test data, <math id="S4.SS4.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\mathbf{x}_{i}\mid\mathbf{x}_{i}\in\mathcal{D}_{\text{test}}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mtext>test</mtext></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\mathbf{x}_{i}\mid\mathbf{x}_{i}\in\mathcal{D}_{\text{test}}\}</annotation></semantics></math> have no overlap. This separation prevents data leakage from steering vectors training to their evaluation on independently and identically distributed (i.i.d.) test samples. By ensuring that the model has not encountered any of the test samples during its training, I can obtain a more reliable estimate of the in-distribution generalization. The out-of–distribution (OOD) generalization of steering vectors has previously been evaluated in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tan et al. (2024)</a></cite>. If not stated otherwise, I choose <math id="S4.SS4.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{N}_{\text{train}}=250" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ℕ</mi><mtext>train</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>250</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{N}_{\text{train}}=250</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS4.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{N}_{\text{test}}=500" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ℕ</mi><mtext>test</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>500</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{N}_{\text{test}}=500</annotation></semantics></math> by default.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SSx1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">Output logits and probabilities</h3>

<div id="S4.SSx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SSx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To measure the effect size, I let the model generate an answer token logit distribution, once <em id="S4.SSx1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">with</em> and once <em id="S4.SSx1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">without</em> applying steering to measure the counterfactual impact of the intervention. For each prompt <math id="S4.SSx1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, the Transformer model generates a final contextual output vector <math id="S4.SSx1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{u}(\mathbf{x}_{i})\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{e}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝐮</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi></msub></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{u}(\mathbf{x}_{i})\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{e}}</annotation></semantics></math>. When steering is applied (e.g., by adding <math id="S4.SSx1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda\cdot\mathbf{s}^{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msup><mi>𝐬</mi><mi>l</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda\cdot\mathbf{s}^{l}</annotation></semantics></math> to the activations <math id="S4.SSx1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{a}^{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝐚</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{a}^{l}</annotation></semantics></math> at relevant layers <math id="S4.SSx1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>l</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l</annotation></semantics></math>), the modified final contextual output vector is denoted <math id="S4.SSx1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{u}^{\text{steered}}(\mathbf{x}_{i})\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{e}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>𝐮</mi><mtext>steered</mtext></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi></msub></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{u}^{\text{steered}}(\mathbf{x}_{i})\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{e}}</annotation></semantics></math>. The output vector is then transformed by the unembedding matrix <math id="S4.SSx1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{u}\in\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}_{V}\times d_{e}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><msub><mi>ℕ</mi><mi>V</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{u}\in\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}_{V}\times d_{e}}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S4.SSx1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{N}_{V}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ℕ</mi><mi>V</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{N}_{V}</annotation></semantics></math> is the vocabulary size. The resulting vector <math id="S4.SSx1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{u}\mathbf{u}(\mathbf{x}_{i})\in\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}_{V}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>ℕ</mi><mi>V</mi></msub></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{u}\mathbf{u}(\mathbf{x}_{i})\in\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}_{V}}</annotation></semantics></math> assigns a real value, the logit, to every token in the vocabulary. The corresponding output probability distribution over the vocabulary, denoted as <math id="S4.SSx1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{p}(\mathbf{x}_{i})\in\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}_{V}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝐩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>ℕ</mi><mi>V</mi></msub></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{p}(\mathbf{x}_{i})\in\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}_{V}}</annotation></semantics></math>, is obtained by applying the softmax function to these logits:</p>
<table id="S4.Ex4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{p}(\mathbf{x}_{i})=\text{softmax}\left(W_{u}\mathbf{u}(\mathbf{x}_{i})\right)" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝐩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mtext>softmax</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{p}(\mathbf{x}_{i})=\text{softmax}\left(W_{u}\mathbf{u}(\mathbf{x}_{i})\right)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SSx1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">The <math id="S4.SSx1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>-th component of <math id="S4.SSx1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{p}(\mathbf{x}_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{p}(\mathbf{x}_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> is the estimated probability of the <math id="S4.SSx1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>-th token being the next token.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SSx1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SSx1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Analogously, applying steering to the model activations during inference on the prompt <math id="S4.SSx1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{x}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{x}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> generates the steered contextual output vector <math id="S4.SSx1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{u}^{\text{steered}}(\mathbf{x}_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐮</mi><mtext>steered</mtext></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{u}^{\text{steered}}(\mathbf{x}_{i})</annotation></semantics></math>. Applying the unembedding matrix obtains the vector of output logits <math id="S4.SSx1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{u}\mathbf{u}^{\text{steered}}(\mathbf{x}_{i})\in\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}_{V}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>𝐮</mi><mtext>steered</mtext></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>ℕ</mi><mi>V</mi></msub></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{u}\mathbf{u}^{\text{steered}}(\mathbf{x}_{i})\in\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}_{V}}</annotation></semantics></math>. The corresponding steered output probability distribution over the vocabulary is denoted as <math id="S4.SSx1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{p}^{\mathrm{steered}}(\mathbf{x}_{i})=\operatorname{softmax}\bigl(W_{u}\,\mathbf{u}^{\mathrm{steered}}(\mathbf{x}_{i})\bigr)\in\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}_{V}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>𝐩</mi><mi>steered</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>softmax</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>𝐮</mi><mi>steered</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>ℕ</mi><mi>V</mi></msub></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{p}^{\mathrm{steered}}(\mathbf{x}_{i})=\operatorname{softmax}\bigl(W_{u}\,\mathbf{u}^{\mathrm{steered}}(\mathbf{x}_{i})\bigr)\in\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}_{V}}</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SSx1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SSx1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">To simplify notation further, I use <math id="S4.SSx1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{logit}(y^{+})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>logit</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{logit}(y^{+})</annotation></semantics></math> to denote the logit value of the answer matching token <math id="S4.SSx1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y^{+}</annotation></semantics></math>. Specifically, <math id="S4.SSx1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{logit}(y^{+})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>logit</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{logit}(y^{+})</annotation></semantics></math> refers to the component of the logit vector <math id="S4.SSx1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{u}\mathbf{u}(\mathbf{x}_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{u}\mathbf{u}(\mathbf{x}_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> that corresponds to the token <math id="S4.SSx1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y^{+}</annotation></semantics></math>. If <math id="S4.SSx1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y^{+}</annotation></semantics></math> is the <math id="S4.SSx1.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>-th token in the vocabulary, then <math id="S4.SSx1.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{logit}(y^{+})=[W_{u}\mathbf{u}(\mathbf{x}_{i})]_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mtext>logit</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐮</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{logit}(y^{+})=[W_{u}\mathbf{u}(\mathbf{x}_{i})]_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Analogously, <math id="S4.SSx1.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{logit}^{\text{steered}}(y^{+})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mtext>logit</mtext><mtext>steered</mtext></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{logit}^{\text{steered}}(y^{+})</annotation></semantics></math> would be the component of the steered logit vector <math id="S4.SSx1.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{u}\mathbf{u}^{\text{steered}}(\mathbf{x}_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>𝐮</mi><mtext>steered</mtext></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{u}\mathbf{u}^{\text{steered}}(\mathbf{x}_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> corresponding to the token <math id="S4.SSx1.p3.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y^{+}</annotation></semantics></math>, i.e., <math id="S4.SSx1.p3.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[W_{u}\mathbf{u}^{\text{steered}}(\mathbf{x}_{i})]_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>u</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>𝐮</mi><mtext>steered</mtext></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[W_{u}\mathbf{u}^{\text{steered}}(\mathbf{x}_{i})]_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SSx1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SSx1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">I follow <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tan et al. (2024)</a></cite> in using the <span id="S4.SSx1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">logit-difference propensity metric</span>:</p>
<table id="S4.Ex5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{LD}(x_{i})=\text{logit}(y^{+})-\text{logit}(y^{-})\text{ , }m_{LD}^{\text{steered}}(x_{i})=\text{logit}^{\text{steered}}(y^{+})-\text{logit}^{\text{steered}}(y^{-})\in\mathbb{R}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>m</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mtext>logit</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mtext>logit</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext> , </mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>m</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow><mtext>steered</mtext></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mtext>logit</mtext><mtext>steered</mtext></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msup><mtext>logit</mtext><mtext>steered</mtext></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℝ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{LD}(x_{i})=\text{logit}(y^{+})-\text{logit}(y^{-})\text{ , }m_{LD}^{\text{steered}}(x_{i})=\text{logit}^{\text{steered}}(y^{+})-\text{logit}^{\text{steered}}(y^{-})\in\mathbb{R}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SSx1.p4.2" class="ltx_p">Based on this, I use three metrics to capture different perspectives on the efficacy and reliability of steering vectors.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SSx1.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">4.4.1 </span>Steering effect size</h4>

<div id="S4.SSx1.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SSx1.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">I measure the <span id="S4.SSx1.SSS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">steering effect size</span> as the difference in the logit-difference propensity between logits <em id="S4.SSx1.SSS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">with</em> and <em id="S4.SSx1.SSS1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">without</em> applied steering vectors:</p>
<table id="S4.Ex6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta m_{LD}(x_{i})=m_{LD}^{\text{steered}}(x_{i})-m_{LD}(x_{i})" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>m</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow><mtext>steered</mtext></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>m</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta m_{LD}(x_{i})=m_{LD}^{\text{steered}}(x_{i})-m_{LD}(x_{i})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SSx1.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">4.4.2 </span>Steering reliability</h4>

<div id="S4.SSx1.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SSx1.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To quantify steering reliability, I measure the <span id="S4.SSx1.SSS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">fraction of anti-steerable samples</span> for which steering negatively impacts the <math id="S4.SSx1.SSS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{LD}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>m</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{LD}</annotation></semantics></math> compared to no steering:</p>
<table id="S4.Ex7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P(\Delta m_{LD}(x_{i})&lt;0)" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P(\Delta m_{LD}(x_{i})&lt;0)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SSx1.SSS3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">4.4.3 </span>Steerability rank</h4>

<div id="S4.SSx1.SSS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SSx1.SSS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To summarize overall steering effectiveness, I adopt the <span id="S4.SSx1.SSS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">steerability score</span> <math id="S4.SSx1.SSS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> from <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tan et al. (2024)</a></cite>. This involves generating a propensity curve by plotting the mean logit-difference over the test set <math id="S4.SSx1.SSS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}_{\text{test}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mtext>test</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}_{\text{test}}</annotation></semantics></math>, denoted <math id="S4.SSx1.SSS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{m}_{LD}(\lambda_{k})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>m</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{m}_{LD}(\lambda_{k})</annotation></semantics></math>, against various steering multipliers <math id="S4.SSx1.SSS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> from the set <math id="S4.SSx1.SSS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Lambda=\{-1.5,-1.0,-0.5,0.0,0.5,1.0,1.5\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1.5</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1.0</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>0.0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1.0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1.5</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Lambda=\{-1.5,-1.0,-0.5,0.0,0.5,1.0,1.5\}</annotation></semantics></math>).
The mean logit-difference for a given multiplier <math id="S4.SSx1.SSS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> is:</p>
<table id="S4.Ex8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{m}_{LD}(\lambda_{k})=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{D}_{\text{test}}|}\sum_{x_{i}\in\mathcal{D}_{\text{test}}}m_{LD}^{\text{steered}}(x_{i},\lambda_{k})" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>m</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mtext>test</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mtext>test</mtext></msub></mrow></munder><mrow><msubsup><mi>m</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow><mtext>steered</mtext></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{m}_{LD}(\lambda_{k})=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{D}_{\text{test}}|}\sum_{x_{i}\in\mathcal{D}_{\text{test}}}m_{LD}^{\text{steered}}(x_{i},\lambda_{k})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SSx1.SSS3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.SSx1.SSS3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{LD}^{\text{steered}}(x_{i},\lambda_{k})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>m</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow><mtext>steered</mtext></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{LD}^{\text{steered}}(x_{i},\lambda_{k})</annotation></semantics></math> is the logit-difference for the sample <math id="S4.SSx1.SSS3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> when the steering vector <math id="S4.SSx1.SSS3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{s}^{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝐬</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{s}^{l}</annotation></semantics></math> is applied with the multiplier <math id="S4.SSx1.SSS3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>. The steerability score <math id="S4.SSx1.SSS3.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> is the slope of the least-squares linear regression line fitted to the <math id="S4.SSx1.SSS3.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\lambda_{k},\bar{m}_{LD}(\lambda_{k}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>m</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\lambda_{k},\bar{m}_{LD}(\lambda_{k}))</annotation></semantics></math> points of the propensity curve. A higher score <math id="S4.SSx1.SSS3.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> indicates more effective steering. The <span id="S4.SSx1.SSS3.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">steerability rank</span> of a dataset is then determined by sorting datasets based on their steerability scores, allowing for a comparative assessment of how well different behaviors can be steered. In many figures I color code datasets by steerability rank, showing low ranks in green to indicate high steerability scores and high ranks in red to indicate low steerability scores. Throughout the thesis, the terms “steerability” and “steerable” refer collectively to both the steering effect size and its reliability.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.5 </span>Directional agreement</h3>

<div id="S4.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">I measure the directional agreement between two activations <math id="S4.SS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{1},a_{2}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{e}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi></msub></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{1},a_{2}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{e}}</annotation></semantics></math> as the cosine similarity between two vectors:</p>
<table id="S4.Ex9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{cos\_sim}(a_{1},a_{2})=\frac{a_{1}\cdot a_{2}}{\|a_{1}\|\|a_{2}\|}=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_{1i}a_{2i}}{\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_{1i}^{2}}\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_{2i}^{2}}}\in[-1,1]" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mtext>cos_sim</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></msubsup><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><mrow><msqrt><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></msubsup><msubsup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></msqrt><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msqrt><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></msubsup><msubsup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></msqrt></mrow></mfrac><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{cos\_sim}(a_{1},a_{2})=\frac{a_{1}\cdot a_{2}}{\|a_{1}\|\|a_{2}\|}=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_{1i}a_{2i}}{\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_{1i}^{2}}\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_{2i}^{2}}}\in[-1,1]</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS5.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.SS5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\cdot" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>⋅</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cdot</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the dot product, and <math id="S4.SS5.p1.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\|\cdot\|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo rspace="0em">∥</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo lspace="0em">∥</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\cdot\|</annotation></semantics></math> is the Euclidean norm. The maximum value of 1, means full alignment, that <math id="S4.SS5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{1}=\alpha\cdot a_{2}\text{ , for some }\alpha&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext> , for some </mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{1}=\alpha\cdot a_{2}\text{ , for some }\alpha&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>. A cosine similarity of 0 means the activations are orthogonal <math id="S4.SS5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{1}\perp a_{2}\iff\text{cos\_sim}(a_{1},a_{2})=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>⟂</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">⇔</mo><mrow><mrow><mtext>cos_sim</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{1}\perp a_{2}\iff\text{cos\_sim}(a_{1},a_{2})=0</annotation></semantics></math>. A value of -1 means they point in exactly the opposite direction, so <math id="S4.SS5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{1}=\alpha\cdot a_{2}\text{ , for some }\alpha&lt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext> , for some </mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{1}=\alpha\cdot a_{2}\text{ , for some }\alpha&lt;0</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">To quantify the directional agreement between the individual activation differences <math id="S4.SS5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta^{l}(\mathbf{x}_{i},y^{+}_{i},y^{-}_{i})=\mathbf{a}^{l}(\mathbf{x}_{i},y^{+}_{i})-\mathbf{a}^{l}(\mathbf{x}_{i},y^{-}_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>𝐚</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msup><mi>𝐚</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta^{l}(\mathbf{x}_{i},y^{+}_{i},y^{-}_{i})=\mathbf{a}^{l}(\mathbf{x}_{i},y^{+}_{i})-\mathbf{a}^{l}(\mathbf{x}_{i},y^{-}_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> and the steering vector <math id="S4.SS5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{s}^{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝐬</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{s}^{l}</annotation></semantics></math>, I use cosine similarity. This metric captures directional agreement and, unlike distance based measures, it is insensitive to differences in vector norms. The resulting cosine similarity thus directly reflects how well the steering vector approximates each individual activation difference direction.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F5" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.17881v1/steering_vector_directional_agreement_comparison.svg" id="S4.F5.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/219;" width="476" height="219"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F5.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 5</span>: </span><span id="S4.F5.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Mean cosine similarity between the activation differences and the resulting steering vector provides a concise metric to quantify how well, on average, the steering vector aligns directionally with each individual activation differences. The directional agreement metric captures whether the activation differences point into the same direction and are well directionally approximated by a common steering vector. While the computation of the steering vector itself is insensitive to how activations are paired, the mean cosine similarity metric remains sensitive to those pairings.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS5.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS5.p3.1" class="ltx_p">To visualize the overall directional agreement between paired activation differences themselves (pairwise similarities) or the steering vector (steering vector similarities), I use:</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS5.p4" class="ltx_para">
<ol id="S4.I4" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S4.I4.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S4.I4.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I4.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I4.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Pairwise similarities:</span></p>
<table id="S4.Ex10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<li id="S4.I4.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S4.I4.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I4.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I4.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Steering vector similarities:</span></p>

</div>
<div id="S4.SS5.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS5.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Visualizing these distributions highlights both outliers and the overall variance in cosine similarity. A narrow, high-mean <math id="S4.SS5.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{mean}}^{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mi>mean</mi><mi>l</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{mean}}^{l}</annotation></semantics></math> indicates consistent alignment to the steering vector, while a large variance would reflect heterogeneity among activation-difference directions.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.6 </span>Difference-of-means line</h3>

<div id="S4.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Formally, let <math id="S4.SS6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{a}^{l}(x,y^{+})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐚</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{a}^{l}(x,y^{+})</annotation></semantics></math> represent the activation at layer <math id="S4.SS6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>l</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l</annotation></semantics></math> for a given prompt <math id="S4.SS6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> and behavior matching answer token <math id="S4.SS6.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y^{+}</annotation></semantics></math>, and let <math id="S4.SS6.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{a}^{l}(x,y^{-})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐚</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{a}^{l}(x,y^{-})</annotation></semantics></math> represent the activation for the same prompt <math id="S4.SS6.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> and the behavior non-matching answer token <math id="S4.SS6.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y^{-}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y^{-}</annotation></semantics></math>. The positive mean <math id="S4.SS6.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝝁</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">+</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,+}</annotation></semantics></math> and negative mean <math id="S4.SS6.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝝁</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">+</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,+}</annotation></semantics></math> are defined as:</p>
<table id="S4.Ex13" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,+}=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{D}_{\text{train}}|}\sum_{(x,y^{+},y^{-})\in\mathcal{D}_{\text{train}}}\mathbf{a}^{l}(x,y^{+}),\quad\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,-}=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{D}_{\text{train}}|}\sum_{(x,y^{+},y^{-})\in\mathcal{D}_{\text{train}}}\mathbf{a}^{l}(x,y^{-})" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>𝝁</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">+</mo></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mtext>train</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mtext>train</mtext></msub></mrow></munder><mrow><msup><mi>𝐚</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><msup><mi>𝝁</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mtext>train</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mtext>train</mtext></msub></mrow></munder><mrow><msup><mi>𝐚</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,+}=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{D}_{\text{train}}|}\sum_{(x,y^{+},y^{-})\in\mathcal{D}_{\text{train}}}\mathbf{a}^{l}(x,y^{+}),\quad\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,-}=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{D}_{\text{train}}|}\sum_{(x,y^{+},y^{-})\in\mathcal{D}_{\text{train}}}\mathbf{a}^{l}(x,y^{-})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS6.p1.2" class="ltx_p">The <span id="S4.SS6.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">difference-of-means line</span> at layer <math id="S4.SS6.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>l</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l</annotation></semantics></math>, denoted as <math id="S4.SS6.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{doml}^{l}(\mu^{+},\mu^{-})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mtext>doml</mtext><mi>l</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>μ</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>μ</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{doml}^{l}(\mu^{+},\mu^{-})</annotation></semantics></math>, is the infinite line passing through the positive mean <math id="S4.SS6.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝝁</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">+</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,+}</annotation></semantics></math> and negative mean <math id="S4.SS6.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,-}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝝁</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,-}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The positive and negative mean also provide an alternative definition of the steering vector <math id="S4.SS6.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{s}^{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝐬</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{s}^{l}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS6.p3" class="ltx_para">
<table id="S4.Ex14" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{steering vector }\mathbf{s}^{l}=\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,+}-\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,-},\quad\text{mean of all activations }\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l}=\frac{\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,+}+\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,-}}{2}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mtext>steering vector </mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>𝐬</mi><mi>l</mi></msup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>𝝁</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">+</mo></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>𝝁</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><mtext>mean of all activations </mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>l</mi></msup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>𝝁</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">+</mo></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>𝝁</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo></mrow></msup></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{steering vector }\mathbf{s}^{l}=\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,+}-\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,-},\quad\text{mean of all activations }\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l}=\frac{\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,+}+\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,-}}{2}</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</table>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS6.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS6.p4.1" class="ltx_p">I visualize the distribution and discriminability of positive and negative activations along the steering direction by projecting the activations onto the difference-of-means line. To establish a convenient coordinate system, I use parameter <math id="S4.SS6.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa\in\mathbb{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℝ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa\in\mathbb{R}</annotation></semantics></math> to establish:</p>
<table id="S4.Ex15" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{doml}^{l}(\mu^{+},\mu^{-})=\frac{1+\kappa}{2}\cdot\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,+}+\frac{1-\kappa}{2}\cdot\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,-}=\frac{\kappa}{2}\cdot\mathbf{s}^{l}+\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l},\quad\kappa\in\mathbb{R}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mtext>doml</mtext><mi>l</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>μ</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>μ</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>κ</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msup><mi>𝝁</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">+</mo></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>κ</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msup><mi>𝝁</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mi>κ</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msup><mi>𝐬</mi><mi>l</mi></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>l</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℝ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{doml}^{l}(\mu^{+},\mu^{-})=\frac{1+\kappa}{2}\cdot\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,+}+\frac{1-\kappa}{2}\cdot\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,-}=\frac{\kappa}{2}\cdot\mathbf{s}^{l}+\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l},\quad\kappa\in\mathbb{R}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS6.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS6.p5.1" class="ltx_p">The formulation on the left emphasizes the line as a weighted average of <math id="S4.SS6.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,-}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝝁</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,-}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS6.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝝁</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">+</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,+}</annotation></semantics></math>, and is equivalent to the standard line parameterization <math id="S4.SS6.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha\cdot\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,+}+(1-\alpha)\cdot\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,-}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msup><mi>𝝁</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">+</mo></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msup><mi>𝝁</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha\cdot\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,+}+(1-\alpha)\cdot\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,-}</annotation></semantics></math> by setting <math id="S4.SS6.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=(1+\kappa)/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>κ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=(1+\kappa)/2</annotation></semantics></math>. The formulation on the right emphasizes the difference-of-means line as the line that defines the overall mean as its origin and the steering direction as its direction.
This specific parameterization is chosen such that <math id="S4.SS6.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa=-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa=-1</annotation></semantics></math> corresponds to <math id="S4.SS6.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,-}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝝁</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,-}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS6.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa=1</annotation></semantics></math> corresponds to <math id="S4.SS6.p5.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝝁</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">+</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,+}</annotation></semantics></math>, providing an intuitive mapping along the line.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS6.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS6.p6.1" class="ltx_p">The projection of an activation vector <math id="S4.SS6.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{a}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{e}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐚</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi></msub></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{a}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{e}}</annotation></semantics></math> onto the difference-of-means line at layer <math id="S4.SS6.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>l</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l</annotation></semantics></math> can be defined as follows. The difference-of-means line passes through the mean activation <math id="S4.SS6.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l}</annotation></semantics></math> and is in the direction of the steering vector <math id="S4.SS6.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{s}^{l}=\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,+}-\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,-}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐬</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>𝝁</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">+</mo></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>𝝁</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{s}^{l}=\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,+}-\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,-}</annotation></semantics></math>.
