Assuming <math id="S4.SS6.p6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{s}^{l}\neq\mathbf{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐬</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><mo>≠</mo><mn>𝟎</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{s}^{l}\neq\mathbf{0}</annotation></semantics></math>, the projection of the vector <math id="S4.SS6.p6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐚</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{a}</annotation></semantics></math> onto this line, denoted as <math id="S4.SS6.p6.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{proj}_{\text{doml}^{l}}(\mathbf{a})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mtext>proj</mtext><msup><mtext>doml</mtext><mi>l</mi></msup></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐚</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{proj}_{\text{doml}^{l}}(\mathbf{a})</annotation></semantics></math>, is:</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS6.p7" class="ltx_para">
<table id="S4.Ex16" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex16.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{proj}_{\text{doml}^{l}}(\mathbf{a})=\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l}+\frac{(\mathbf{a}-\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l})\cdot\mathbf{s}^{l}}{\|\mathbf{s}^{l}\|^{2}}\mathbf{s}^{l}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mtext>proj</mtext><msup><mtext>doml</mtext><mi>l</mi></msup></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐚</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><mo>+</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>𝐚</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>l</mi></msup></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msup><mi>𝐬</mi><mi>l</mi></msup></mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msup><mi>𝐬</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>𝐬</mi><mi>l</mi></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{proj}_{\text{doml}^{l}}(\mathbf{a})=\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l}+\frac{(\mathbf{a}-\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l})\cdot\mathbf{s}^{l}}{\|\mathbf{s}^{l}\|^{2}}\mathbf{s}^{l}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS6.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS6.p8.1" class="ltx_p">Where <math id="S4.SS6.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\mathbf{s}^{l}\|^{2}=\mathbf{s}^{l}\cdot\mathbf{s}^{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msup><mi>𝐬</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>𝐬</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msup><mi>𝐬</mi><mi>l</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\mathbf{s}^{l}\|^{2}=\mathbf{s}^{l}\cdot\mathbf{s}^{l}</annotation></semantics></math> is the squared Euclidean norm of the steering vector <math id="S4.SS6.p8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{s}^{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝐬</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{s}^{l}</annotation></semantics></math>. This projected vector, <math id="S4.SS6.p8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{proj}_{\text{doml}^{l}}(\mathbf{a})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mtext>proj</mtext><msup><mtext>doml</mtext><mi>l</mi></msup></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐚</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{proj}_{\text{doml}^{l}}(\mathbf{a})</annotation></semantics></math>, is the point on the difference-of-means line that is closest to the point <math id="S4.SS6.p8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐚</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{a}</annotation></semantics></math>. The scalar coefficient <math id="S4.SS6.p8.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{(\mathbf{a}-\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l})\cdot\mathbf{s}^{l}}{\|\mathbf{s}^{l}\|^{2}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>𝐚</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>l</mi></msup></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msup><mi>𝐬</mi><mi>l</mi></msup></mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msup><mi>𝐬</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{(\mathbf{a}-\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l})\cdot\mathbf{s}^{l}}{\|\mathbf{s}^{l}\|^{2}}</annotation></semantics></math> determines where the projection lies along the line relative to <math id="S4.SS6.p8.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l}</annotation></semantics></math> in the direction of <math id="S4.SS6.p8.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{s}^{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝐬</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{s}^{l}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Relating this to the parameterized form of the line <math id="S4.SS6.p8.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{doml}^{l}(\kappa)=\frac{\kappa}{2}\cdot\mathbf{s}^{l}+\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mtext>doml</mtext><mi>l</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>κ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mi>κ</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msup><mi>𝐬</mi><mi>l</mi></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>l</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{doml}^{l}(\kappa)=\frac{\kappa}{2}\cdot\mathbf{s}^{l}+\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l}</annotation></semantics></math>, the projection <math id="S4.SS6.p8.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{proj}_{\text{doml}^{l}}(\mathbf{a})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mtext>proj</mtext><msup><mtext>doml</mtext><mi>l</mi></msup></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐚</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{proj}_{\text{doml}^{l}}(\mathbf{a})</annotation></semantics></math> corresponds to a specific value of <math id="S4.SS6.p8.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math> for the vector <math id="S4.SS6.p8.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐚</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{a}</annotation></semantics></math>, which can be denoted:</p>
<table id="S4.Ex17" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex17.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa_{\mathbf{a}}=2\cdot\frac{(\mathbf{a}-\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l})\cdot\mathbf{s}^{l}}{\|\mathbf{s}^{l}\|^{2}}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>κ</mi><mi>𝐚</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>𝐚</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>𝝁</mi><mi>l</mi></msup></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msup><mi>𝐬</mi><mi>l</mi></msup></mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msup><mi>𝐬</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa_{\mathbf{a}}=2\cdot\frac{(\mathbf{a}-\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l})\cdot\mathbf{s}^{l}}{\|\mathbf{s}^{l}\|^{2}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS6.p9" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS6.p9.1" class="ltx_p">If the steering direction accurately approximates the latent behavior representation and the representation satisfies linearity <a href="#S2.SS4" title="2.4 Linear Representation Hypothesis ‣ 2 Background" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.4</span></a>, universality <a href="#S2.SS4.SSS1" title="2.4.1 Universality of feature directions ‣ 2.4 Linear Representation Hypothesis ‣ 2 Background" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.4.1</span></a>, and scalability <a href="#S2.SS4.SSS2" title="2.4.2 Scalability: Feature strength is encoded by magnitude ‣ 2.4 Linear Representation Hypothesis ‣ 2 Background" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.4.2</span></a>, then <math id="S4.SS6.p9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa_{\mathbf{a}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>κ</mi><mi>𝐚</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa_{\mathbf{a}}</annotation></semantics></math> can be meaningfully interpreted. A positive <math id="S4.SS6.p9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa_{\mathbf{a}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>κ</mi><mi>𝐚</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa_{\mathbf{a}}</annotation></semantics></math> means the activation is likely interpreted as exhibiting the target (positive) behavior, with larger <math id="S4.SS6.p9.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math> values corresponding to a stronger expression of that behavior. Conversely, <math id="S4.SS6.p9.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa_{\mathbf{a}}&lt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>κ</mi><mi>𝐚</mi></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa_{\mathbf{a}}&lt;0</annotation></semantics></math> indicates the model’s representation is tilted toward the negative behavior state, and <math id="S4.SS6.p9.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa_{\mathbf{a}}&gt;1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>κ</mi><mi>𝐚</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa_{\mathbf{a}}&gt;1</annotation></semantics></math> reflects an even more pronounced positive encoding beyond the training mean.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
<figure id="S4.F6" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">
<figure id="S4.F6.sf1" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.17881v1/difference_of_means_line_conceptual_plot_well_separable_with_classification_boundary.svg" id="S4.F6.sf1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/325;" width="476" height="325"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F6.sf1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">(a)</span> </span><span id="S4.F6.sf1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Positive and negative activations are well separated along the difference-of-means line and are separable with a classification boundary orthogonal to it.</span></figcaption>
</figure></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">
<figure id="S4.F6.sf2" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.17881v1/difference_of_means_line_skewed_gaussian_conceptual_plot.svg" id="S4.F6.sf2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/325;" width="476" height="325"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F6.sf2.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">(b)</span> </span><span id="S4.F6.sf2.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Positive and negative activations overlap considerably along the difference-of-means line, but are relatively well separable by a linear classifier.</span></figcaption>
</figure></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F6.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 6</span>: </span><span id="S4.F6.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">In (a) and (b), the positive and negative activations are shown in a 2D subspace at the top. The bottom shows the same activations projected onto the difference-of-means line. The d’ values are the discriminability index, explained in Section <a href="#S4.SS9.SSS1" title="4.9.1 Discriminability index ‣ 4.9 Separability metrics ‣ 4 Methods and Experimental Setup" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.9.1</span></a>, which measures separability along the difference-of-means line (high values mean high separability).</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS6.p10" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS6.p10.1" class="ltx_p">To verify if separability across the difference-of-means line generalizes to other projections, I also evaluate separability across two common linear classifiers: Linear Discriminant Analysis and a logistic regression classifier.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS7" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.7 </span>Logistic regression probe</h3>

<div id="S4.SS7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A logistic regression probe is used to identify a linear direction in the activation space optimized for classifying activations as originating from positive (<math id="S4.SS7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y^{+}</annotation></semantics></math>) or negative (<math id="S4.SS7.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y^{-}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y^{-}</annotation></semantics></math>) samples.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS7.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Probe direction and projection</h5>

<div id="S4.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The probe is trained on layer <math id="S4.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>l</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l</annotation></semantics></math> activations from <math id="S4.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}_{\text{train}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mtext>train</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}_{\text{train}}</annotation></semantics></math>, where positive activations <math id="S4.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{a}^{l}(x_{i},y^{+}_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐚</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{a}^{l}(x_{i},y^{+}_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> are labeled 1 and negative activations <math id="S4.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{a}^{l}(x_{i},y^{-}_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐚</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{a}^{l}(x_{i},y^{-}_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> are labeled 0. The trained logistic regression model yields a weight vector <math id="S4.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{w}_{\text{logreg}}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{e}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐰</mi><mtext>logreg</mtext></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi></msub></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{w}_{\text{logreg}}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{e}}</annotation></semantics></math>, which defines the <span id="S4.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">logistic regression probe direction</span>. An activation <math id="S4.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐚</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{a}</annotation></semantics></math> is projected onto this direction via the dot product: <math id="S4.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{proj}_{\text{logreg}}(\mathbf{a})=\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{w}_{\text{logreg}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mtext>proj</mtext><mtext>logreg</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐚</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝐚</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>𝐰</mi><mtext>logreg</mtext></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{proj}_{\text{logreg}}(\mathbf{a})=\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{w}_{\text{logreg}}</annotation></semantics></math>. These scalar projections are used to visualize distributions and assess separability (e.g., via <math id="S4.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>d</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> in Section <a href="#S4.SS9.SSS1" title="4.9.1 Discriminability index ‣ 4.9 Separability metrics ‣ 4 Methods and Experimental Setup" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.9.1</span></a> or other metrics in Section <a href="#S4.SS9" title="4.9 Separability metrics ‣ 4 Methods and Experimental Setup" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.9</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS7.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Relevance and comparison to difference-of-means line</h5>

<div id="S4.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Unlike the difference-of-means line (<math id="S4.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{s}^{l}=\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,+}-\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,-}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐬</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>𝝁</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">+</mo></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>𝝁</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{s}^{l}=\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,+}-\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,-}</annotation></semantics></math>), which is based solely on class centroids, the <math id="S4.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{w}_{\text{logreg}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐰</mi><mtext>logreg</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{w}_{\text{logreg}}</annotation></semantics></math> direction is learned by optimizing a classification objective across all training activations. It can therefore find a direction offering superior class separation, particularly if distributions are not best separated by their means. The logistic regression probe highlights a data-driven, classification-optimized view of behavioral encoding.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS8" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.8 </span>Linear Discriminant Analysis</h3>

<div id="S4.SS8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) provides another method to find a linear projection direction that best separates positive and negative activations at layer <math id="S4.SS8.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>l</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS8.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">LDA principle and direction</h5>

<div id="S4.SS8.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS8.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">LDA seeks a direction <math id="S4.SS8.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{w}_{\text{LDA}}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{e}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐰</mi><mtext>LDA</mtext></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi></msub></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{w}_{\text{LDA}}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{e}}</annotation></semantics></math> that maximizes the ratio of between-class variance to within-class variance of the projected activations. This direction is given by <math id="S4.SS8.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{w}_{\text{LDA}}\propto\Sigma_{W}^{-1}(\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,+}-\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,-})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐰</mi><mtext>LDA</mtext></msub><mo>∝</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mi>W</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>𝝁</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">+</mo></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>𝝁</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo></mrow></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{w}_{\text{LDA}}\propto\Sigma_{W}^{-1}(\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,+}-\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,-})</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S4.SS8.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝝁</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">+</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,+}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS8.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,-}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝝁</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\boldsymbol{\mu}^{l,-}</annotation></semantics></math> are the class means (as defined in Section <a href="#S4.SS6" title="4.6 Difference-of-means line ‣ 4 Methods and Experimental Setup" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.6</span></a>) and <math id="S4.SS8.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma_{W}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mi>W</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma_{W}</annotation></semantics></math> is the pooled within-class covariance matrix derived from the sets of positive activations <math id="S4.SS8.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\mathbf{a}^{l}(x_{i},y^{+}_{i})\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><msup><mi>𝐚</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\mathbf{a}^{l}(x_{i},y^{+}_{i})\}</annotation></semantics></math> and negative activations <math id="S4.SS8.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\mathbf{a}^{l}(x_{i},y^{-}_{i})\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><msup><mi>𝐚</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\mathbf{a}^{l}(x_{i},y^{-}_{i})\}</annotation></semantics></math> in <math id="S4.SS8.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}_{\text{train}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mtext>train</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}_{\text{train}}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS8.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Projection onto the LDA probe direction</h5>

<div id="S4.SS8.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS8.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Activations <math id="S4.SS8.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{a}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{e}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐚</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi></msub></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{a}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{e}}</annotation></semantics></math> are projected onto the LDA direction using the dot product: <math id="S4.SS8.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{proj}_{\text{LDA}}(\mathbf{a})=\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{w}_{\text{LDA}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mtext>proj</mtext><mtext>LDA</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐚</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝐚</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>𝐰</mi><mtext>LDA</mtext></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{proj}_{\text{LDA}}(\mathbf{a})=\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{w}_{\text{LDA}}</annotation></semantics></math>. These projections facilitate visualization and separability analysis using the metrics described in Section <a href="#S4.SS9" title="4.9 Separability metrics ‣ 4 Methods and Experimental Setup" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.9</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS8.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Relevance and comparison to difference-of-means line</h5>

<div id="S4.SS8.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS8.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">LDA offers a statistically motivated direction for class separation by considering both class means and their covariance structures. If class covariances are equal and spherical, <math id="S4.SS8.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{w}_{\text{LDA}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐰</mi><mtext>LDA</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{w}_{\text{LDA}}</annotation></semantics></math> aligns with the difference-of-means direction <math id="S4.SS8.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{s}^{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝐬</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{s}^{l}</annotation></semantics></math>. However, LDA typically finds a distinct, often more discriminative, direction when covariances differ, as it accounts for the shape and orientation of the activation clusters. LDA probes are valuable for revealing intrinsic separability based on Fisher’s discriminant criterion.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS9" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.9 </span>Separability metrics</h3>

<div id="S4.SS9.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS9.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Once activations are projected onto a 1D line (e.g., the difference-of-means line, a logistic regression probe direction, or an LDA direction), I obtain two sets of scalar values: one for projected positive activations, <math id="S4.SS9.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{P}^{+}=\{\text{proj}(\mathbf{a}^{l}(x_{i},y^{+}_{i}))\}_{i=1}^{|\mathcal{D}_{\text{train}}|}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mtext>proj</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>𝐚</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mtext>train</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{P}^{+}=\{\text{proj}(\mathbf{a}^{l}(x_{i},y^{+}_{i}))\}_{i=1}^{|\mathcal{D}_{\text{train}}|}</annotation></semantics></math>, and one for projected negative activations, <math id="S4.SS9.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{P}^{-}=\{\text{proj}(\mathbf{a}^{l}(x_{i},y^{-}_{i}))\}_{i=1}^{|\mathcal{D}_{\text{train}}|}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mtext>proj</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>𝐚</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mtext>train</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{P}^{-}=\{\text{proj}(\mathbf{a}^{l}(x_{i},y^{-}_{i}))\}_{i=1}^{|\mathcal{D}_{\text{train}}|}</annotation></semantics></math>. I use several metrics to quantify the separability of these two distributions of scalar values.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS9.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">4.9.1 </span>Discriminability index</h4>

<div id="S4.SS9.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS9.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">I can formalize the notion of discriminability by measuring the discriminability index, <math id="S4.SS9.SSS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>d</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math>, between the projected activations as shown in Figure <a href="#S5.F12" title="Figure 12 ‣ 5.5 Separability along the difference-of-means line predicts steerability ‣ 5 Results" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a>. This is a measure of the distance between the means of two distributions, normalized by their standard deviations. The discriminability index <math id="S4.SS9.SSS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>d</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> is calculated as:</p>
<table id="S4.Ex18" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex18.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d^{\prime}=\frac{|\text{mean}(\mathcal{P}^{+})-\text{mean}(\mathcal{P}^{-})|}{\sqrt{\frac{1}{2}(\text{var}(\mathcal{P}^{+})+\text{var}(\mathcal{P}^{-}))}}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mrow><mtext>mean</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mtext>mean</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><msqrt><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mtext>var</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mtext>var</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msqrt></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d^{\prime}=\frac{|\text{mean}(\mathcal{P}^{+})-\text{mean}(\mathcal{P}^{-})|}{\sqrt{\frac{1}{2}(\text{var}(\mathcal{P}^{+})+\text{var}(\mathcal{P}^{-}))}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS9.SSS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.SS9.SSS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{mean}(\mathcal{P}^{+})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>mean</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{mean}(\mathcal{P}^{+})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS9.SSS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{mean}(\mathcal{P}^{-})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>mean</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{mean}(\mathcal{P}^{-})</annotation></semantics></math> are the means of the projected positive and negative activations respectively, and <math id="S4.SS9.SSS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{var}(\mathcal{P}^{+})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>var</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{var}(\mathcal{P}^{+})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS9.SSS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{var}(\mathcal{P}^{-})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>var</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{var}(\mathcal{P}^{-})</annotation></semantics></math> are their respective variances. A higher <math id="S4.SS9.SSS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>d</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> indicates better separation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS9.SSSx1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection">Area Under the ROC Curve (AUROC)</h4>

<div id="S4.SS9.SSSx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS9.SSSx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUROC or AUC) measures the ability of the 1D projected values to discriminate between positive (<math id="S4.SS9.SSSx1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y^{+}</annotation></semantics></math>) and negative (<math id="S4.SS9.SSSx1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y^{-}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y^{-}</annotation></semantics></math>) samples. The ROC curve is a plot of the True Positive Rate (TPR) against the False Positive Rate (FPR) at various classification thresholds.
Let <math id="S4.SS9.SSSx1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mo>+</mo></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{+}</annotation></semantics></math> be the number of positive samples and <math id="S4.SS9.SSSx1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{-}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mo>−</mo></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{-}</annotation></semantics></math> be the number of negative samples.</p>
<table id="S4.Ex19" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex19.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{TPR}=\frac{\text{True Positives}}{\text{Number of Positive Samples ($N_{+}$)}}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>TPR</mtext><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mtext>True Positives</mtext><mrow><mtext>Number of Positive Samples (</mtext><msub><mi>N</mi><mo>+</mo></msub><mtext>)</mtext></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{TPR}=\frac{\text{True Positives}}{\text{Number of Positive Samples ($N_{+}$)}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<table id="S4.Ex20" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex20.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{FPR}=\frac{\text{False Positives}}{\text{Number of Negative Samples ($N_{-}$)}}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>FPR</mtext><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mtext>False Positives</mtext><mrow><mtext>Number of Negative Samples (</mtext><msub><mi>N</mi><mo>−</mo></msub><mtext>)</mtext></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{FPR}=\frac{\text{False Positives}}{\text{Number of Negative Samples ($N_{-}$)}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS9.SSSx1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">The AUROC is the area under this curve.</p>
<ul id="S4.I5" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S4.I5.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I5.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I5.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I5.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">AUROC = 1</span>: Perfect separation; all positive samples have higher projected values than all negative samples (or vice-versa, depending on the direction of separation chosen).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I5.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I5.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I5.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I5.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">AUROC = 0.5</span>: No separation; the projected values offer no discriminatory power, equivalent to random guessing.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I5.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I5.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I5.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I5.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">AUROC &lt; 0.5</span>: The feature separates classes in the opposite direction of what’s expected.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
<p id="S4.SS9.SSSx1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">The AUROC ranges from 0 to 1 and represents the probability that a randomly chosen positive sample is ranked higher (has a higher projected value) than a randomly chosen negative sample, assuming higher values are associated with the positive class.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS9.SSSx2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection">Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) statistic</h4>

<div id="S4.SS9.SSSx2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS9.SSSx2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) statistic quantifies the maximum difference between the cumulative distribution functions (CDFs) of the projected positive and negative activations. Let <math id="S4.SS9.SSSx2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{\mathcal{P}^{+}}(s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>+</mo></msup></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{\mathcal{P}^{+}}(s)</annotation></semantics></math> be the empirical CDF of the projected positive activations <math id="S4.SS9.SSSx2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{P}^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{P}^{+}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS9.SSSx2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{\mathcal{P}^{-}}(s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>−</mo></msup></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{\mathcal{P}^{-}}(s)</annotation></semantics></math> be the empirical CDF of the projected negative activations <math id="S4.SS9.SSSx2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{P}^{-}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{P}^{-}</annotation></semantics></math>. The KS statistic <math id="S4.SS9.SSSx2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math> is defined as:</p>
<table id="S4.Ex21" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex21.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D=\sup_{s}|F_{\mathcal{P}^{+}}(s)-F_{\mathcal{P}^{-}}(s)|" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo rspace="0.1389em">=</mo><mrow><munder><mo lspace="0.1389em" movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">sup</mo><mi>s</mi></munder><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>+</mo></msup></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>−</mo></msup></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D=\sup_{s}|F_{\mathcal{P}^{+}}(s)-F_{\mathcal{P}^{-}}(s)|</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS9.SSSx2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.SS9.SSSx2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sup_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mo>sup</mo><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sup_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> is the supremum over all possible scalar projection values <math id="S4.SS9.SSSx2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
<ul id="S4.I6" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S4.I6.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I6.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I6.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A larger <math id="S4.I6.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math> value indicates a greater separation between the two distributions.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I6.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I6.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I6.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S4.I6.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math> ranges from 0 to 1. <math id="S4.I6.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D=0</annotation></semantics></math> means the two distributions are identical, while <math id="S4.I6.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D=1</annotation></semantics></math> implies no overlap in their CDFs over their observed range (i.e., one distribution is entirely to one side of the other).</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
<p id="S4.SS9.SSSx2.p1.3" class="ltx_p">The KS statistic is non-parametric and sensitive to differences in location, scale, and shape of the distributions.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS9.SSSx3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection">Overlap Coefficient (OVL)</h4>

<div id="S4.SS9.SSSx3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS9.SSSx3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The Overlap Coefficient (OVL) directly quantifies the amount of overlap between the probability density functions (PDFs) of the projected positive and negative activations. Let <math id="S4.SS9.SSSx3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{\mathcal{P}^{+}}(s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>+</mo></msup></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{\mathcal{P}^{+}}(s)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS9.SSSx3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{\mathcal{P}^{-}}(s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>−</mo></msup></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{\mathcal{P}^{-}}(s)</annotation></semantics></math> be the estimated PDFs of the projected positive and negative activations, respectively. The OVL is defined as:</p>
<table id="S4.Ex22" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex22.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{OVL}=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\min(p_{\mathcal{P}^{+}}(s),p_{\mathcal{P}^{-}}(s))ds" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>OVL</mtext><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∫</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msubsup><mrow><mi>min</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>+</mo></msup></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>−</mo></msup></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{OVL}=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\min(p_{\mathcal{P}^{+}}(s),p_{\mathcal{P}^{-}}(s))ds</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<ul id="S4.I7" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S4.I7.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I7.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I7.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I7.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">OVL = 0</span>: No overlap, indicating perfect separation of the two distributions based on the projected values.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I7.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I7.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I7.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I7.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">OVL = 1</span>: The distributions are identical.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
<p id="S4.SS9.SSSx3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">The OVL ranges from 0 to 1. A lower OVL indicates better separability.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS10" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.10 </span>Statistical correlation and significance</h3>

<div id="S4.SS10.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS10.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To analyze relationships between different scalar measures derived from my experiments (e.g., relating separability metrics to steering effect sizes), and to assess the significance of these relationships, I employ standard statistical tools.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS10.SSSx1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection">Pearson correlation coefficient</h4>

<div id="S4.SS10.SSSx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS10.SSSx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The Pearson correlation coefficient (Pearson’s <math id="S4.SS10.SSSx1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>) measures the linear relationship between two continuous variables. For two variables <math id="S4.SS10.SSSx1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X=\{x_{1},\dots,x_{N}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X=\{x_{1},\dots,x_{N}\}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS10.SSSx1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y=\{y_{1},\dots,y_{N}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y=\{y_{1},\dots,y_{N}\}</annotation></semantics></math>, the Pearson correlation coefficient is calculated as:</p>
<table id="S4.Ex23" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex23.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{XY}=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{N}(x_{i}-\bar{x})(y_{i}-\bar{y})}{\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^{N}(x_{i}-\bar{x})^{2}}\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^{N}(y_{i}-\bar{y})^{2}}}=\frac{\text{cov}(X,Y)}{\sigma_{X}\sigma_{Y}}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><mrow><mrow><mo lspace="0em" stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mrow><msqrt><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><msup><mrow><mo lspace="0em" stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msqrt><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><msup><mrow><mo lspace="0em" stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mtext>cov</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>X</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>Y</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{XY}=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{N}(x_{i}-\bar{x})(y_{i}-\bar{y})}{\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^{N}(x_{i}-\bar{x})^{2}}\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^{N}(y_{i}-\bar{y})^{2}}}=\frac{\text{cov}(X,Y)}{\sigma_{X}\sigma_{Y}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS10.SSSx1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.SS10.SSSx1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{x}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{x}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS10.SSSx1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{y}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{y}</annotation></semantics></math> are the means of <math id="S4.SS10.SSSx1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS10.SSSx1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y</annotation></semantics></math>, respectively, <math id="S4.SS10.SSSx1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{cov}(X,Y)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>cov</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{cov}(X,Y)</annotation></semantics></math> is their covariance, and <math id="S4.SS10.SSSx1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>X</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{X}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS10.SSSx1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{Y}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>Y</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{Y}</annotation></semantics></math> are their standard deviations.
The value of <math id="S4.SS10.SSSx1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{XY}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{XY}</annotation></semantics></math> ranges from -1 to 1:</p>
<ul id="S4.I8" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S4.I8.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I8.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I8.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S4.I8.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{XY}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{XY}=1</annotation></semantics></math>: Perfect positive linear correlation.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I8.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I8.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I8.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S4.I8.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{XY}=-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{XY}=-1</annotation></semantics></math>: Perfect negative linear correlation.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I8.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I8.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I8.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S4.I8.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{XY}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{XY}=0</annotation></semantics></math>: No linear correlation.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
<p id="S4.SS10.SSSx1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">Pearson correlation assumes that the data are approximately normally distributed and that the relationship between variables is linear.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS10.SSSx2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection">Spearman rank correlation coefficient</h4>

<div id="S4.SS10.SSSx2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS10.SSSx2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The Spearman rank correlation coefficient (Spearman’s <math id="S4.SS10.SSSx2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ρ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="S4.SS10.SSSx2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{s}</annotation></semantics></math>) assesses the monotonic relationship between two continuous or ordinal variables. It is calculated by first converting the values of each variable into ranks, and then computing the Pearson correlation coefficient on these ranks. For two variables <math id="S4.SS10.SSSx2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS10.SSSx2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y</annotation></semantics></math>, let <math id="S4.SS10.SSSx2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="rg_{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>X</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">rg_{X}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS10.SSSx2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="rg_{Y}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>Y</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">rg_{Y}</annotation></semantics></math> be their respective rank variables. The Spearman correlation is:</p>
<table id="S4.Ex24" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex24.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{s}=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{N}(rg_{x_{i}}-\overline{rg_{X}})(rg_{y_{i}}-\overline{rg_{Y}})}{\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^{N}(rg_{x_{i}}-\overline{rg_{X}})^{2}}\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^{N}(rg_{y_{i}}-\overline{rg_{Y}})^{2}}}=\frac{\text{cov}(rg_{X},rg_{Y})}{\sigma_{rg_{X}}\sigma_{rg_{Y}}}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><mrow><mrow><mo lspace="0em" stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub></mrow><mo>−</mo><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>X</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub></mrow><mo>−</mo><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>Y</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mrow><msqrt><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><msup><mrow><mo lspace="0em" stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub></mrow><mo>−</mo><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>X</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msqrt><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><msup><mrow><mo lspace="0em" stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub></mrow><mo>−</mo><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>Y</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mtext>cov</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>X</mi></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>Y</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>X</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>Y</mi></msub></mrow></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{s}=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{N}(rg_{x_{i}}-\overline{rg_{X}})(rg_{y_{i}}-\overline{rg_{Y}})}{\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^{N}(rg_{x_{i}}-\overline{rg_{X}})^{2}}\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^{N}(rg_{y_{i}}-\overline{rg_{Y}})^{2}}}=\frac{\text{cov}(rg_{X},rg_{Y})}{\sigma_{rg_{X}}\sigma_{rg_{Y}}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS10.SSSx2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">The value of <math id="S4.SS10.SSSx2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> also ranges from -1 to 1:</p>
<ul id="S4.I9" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S4.I9.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I9.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I9.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S4.I9.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{s}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{s}=1</annotation></semantics></math>: Perfect positive monotonic relationship (as one variable increases, the other always increases).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I9.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I9.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I9.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S4.I9.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{s}=-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{s}=-1</annotation></semantics></math>: Perfect negative monotonic relationship (as one variable increases, the other always decreases).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I9.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I9.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I9.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S4.I9.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{s}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{s}=0</annotation></semantics></math>: No monotonic relationship.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
<p id="S4.SS10.SSSx2.p1.3" class="ltx_p">Spearman correlation is non-parametric and does not assume a specific distribution for the data. It is more robust to outliers and can capture non-linear monotonic relationships that Pearson correlation might miss.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS10.SSSx3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection">P-values</h4>

<div id="S4.SS10.SSSx3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS10.SSSx3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A p-value (probability value) is used in the context of null hypothesis significance testing to help decide whether an observed result (e.g., a correlation coefficient being non-zero) is statistically significant. The p-value is the probability of obtaining test results at least as extreme as the results actually observed, under the assumption that the null hypothesis is correct. The null hypothesis (<math id="S4.SS10.SSSx3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>) typically states that there is no effect or no relationship (e.g., the true correlation is zero).</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS10.SSSx3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<ul id="S4.I10" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S4.I10.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I10.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I10.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A small p-value (typically <math id="S4.I10.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\leq 0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≤</mo><mn>0.05</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\leq 0.05</annotation></semantics></math>) indicates strong evidence against the null hypothesis, so you reject the null hypothesis. This suggests that the observed relationship is unlikely to be due to random chance alone.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I10.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I10.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I10.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A large p-value (<math id="S4.I10.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&gt;0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0.05</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&gt;0.05</annotation></semantics></math>) indicates weak evidence against the null hypothesis, so you fail to reject the null hypothesis. This suggests that the observed relationship could plausibly be due to random chance.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS10.SSSx3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS10.SSSx3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">P-values are typically reported alongside correlation coefficients to indicate the statistical significance of the observed correlation. It is important to note that a p-value does not measure the size of an effect or the importance of a result, nor does it provide the probability that the null hypothesis is true.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS11" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.11 </span>Prompt types</h3>

<div id="S4.SS11.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS11.p1.1" class="ltx_p">I evaluate whether changes to the steering vector training prompts impact reliability and steering effect size. An effective training sample elicits model activations that best represent the target behavior. I systematically explore seven distinct prompt types, by varying three components:</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS11.p2" class="ltx_para">
<ul id="S4.I11" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S4.I11.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I11.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I11.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I11.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Prefilled:</span> Whether the final answer token (e.g., "Yes", "No", "A", or "B") is appended. Appending the answer aims to condition the model’s preceding activations on the intended outcome, thereby activating representations linked to producing that specific behavioral output.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I11.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I11.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I11.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I11.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Instruction:</span> Whether an explicit instruction is prepended to the question. The inclusion of instructions is intended to leverage the model’s instruction-following capabilities from instruction tuning <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wei et al., 2022a</a>)</cite>, guiding it to activate the corresponding desired behavior.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I11.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I11.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I11.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I11.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Few-shot:</span> Whether 5-shot demonstration examples are included. By providing examples, I aim to leverage in-context learning (ICL) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Brown et al., 2020b</a>; <a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dong et al., 2024</a>)</cite> to strongly evoke and activate the model’s internal representation of the target behavior.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS11.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS11.p3.1" class="ltx_p">For each of the 36 datasets, I generated behavior-encouraging and behavior-discouraging instructions and few-shot prompts that are available in the Appendix <a href="#A3.SS3" title="C.3 Behavior Matching and Behavior Non-Matching Instructions ‣ Appendix C Datasets and Prompts" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.3</span></a>. These elements are prepended to a base question <math id="S4.SS11.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> to create either a positive prompt <math id="S4.SS11.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^{+}</annotation></semantics></math> (designed to elicit the target behavior) or a negative prompt <math id="S4.SS11.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x^{-}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^{-}</annotation></semantics></math> (designed to elicit the opposite or absence of the behavior). The method of recording activations depends on whether the prompt is prefilled:</p>
<ul id="S4.I12" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S4.I12.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I12.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I12.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In <span id="S4.I12.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">non-prefilled</span> settings, the model processes <math id="S4.I12.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^{+}</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="S4.I12.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x^{-}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^{-}</annotation></semantics></math>. The activations, denoted <math id="S4.I12.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{a}^{l}(x^{+})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐚</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{a}^{l}(x^{+})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.I12.i1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{a}^{l}(x^{-})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐚</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{a}^{l}(x^{-})</annotation></semantics></math> respectively, are recorded at the final token position of the input prompt (i.e., as the model begins to generate an answer). Not prefilling the answer token only makes sense, if behavior encouraging instructions or few-shot samples are prepended.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I12.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I12.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I12.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In <span id="S4.I12.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">prefilled</span> settings, a positive answer token <math id="S4.I12.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y^{+}</annotation></semantics></math> is appended to <math id="S4.I12.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^{+}</annotation></semantics></math>, and a negative answer token <math id="S4.I12.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y^{-}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y^{-}</annotation></semantics></math> is appended to <math id="S4.I12.i2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x^{-}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^{-}</annotation></semantics></math>. Activations, denoted <math id="S4.I12.i2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{a}^{l}(x^{+},y^{+})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐚</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{a}^{l}(x^{+},y^{+})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.I12.i2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{a}^{l}(x^{-},y^{-})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐚</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{a}^{l}(x^{-},y^{-})</annotation></semantics></math>, are recorded at the position of the appended answer token (<math id="S4.I12.i2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y^{+}</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="S4.I12.i2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y^{-}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y^{-}</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS11.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS11.p4.1" class="ltx_p">The various combinations of these components (prefilled, instruction, few-shot) result in the seven distinct prompt types used for training steering vectors. A detailed description of all seven setups, along with examples, is provided in Appendix <a href="#A3" title="Appendix C Datasets and Prompts" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C</span></a>. Importantly, a standardized test prompt format is used for all evaluations, irrespective of the prompt type used for training the steering vector.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Results</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This section presents a series of experiments designed to identify and quantify the properties of model activation patterns that determine the reliability of steering vectors. The analysis demonstrates a statistically significant correlation between steering efficacy and specific characteristics of the activations used for training steering vectors.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The analysis begins in Section <a href="#S5.SS1" title="5.1 Convergence analysis of steering vectors ‣ 5 Results" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.1</span></a> by determining the minimum number of samples needed to compute a stable steering vector, thereby establishing a methodologically sound basis for the experiments that follow. Having established the experimental setup, the subsequent sections address the first research question by identifying and evaluating two statistical predictors for steering reliability.</p>
<ul id="S5.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S5.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
